sources.entry: SyncTube - Lightweight and very simple to setup CyTube alternative to watch videos with friends and chat. MIT Nodejs/Haxe

summary.one_liner: SyncTube is a lightweight, self-hosted web app for watching synchronized videos with friends, with a built-in chat, written in Haxe and run on Node.js.
summary.what_it_does: It keeps video playback in sync across all connected page users, with a "Leader" button that grants global play/pause, seeking and speed control. Users add videos by URL, and it supports YouTube, Twitch, Vimeo, Streamable, VK, Peertube, raw mp4/m3u8 files, and iframes (without sync). A chat includes time-rewind commands such as /30 or /-1h9m54, plus admin commands for banning, kicking and clearing chat. Local video files can be started while still uploading. External vtt/srt/ass subtitles and external audio tracks are supported, and a server-side cache for supported sites is available as an optional feature using ffmpeg/ffprobe. The README also mentions a native mobile client, hotkeys, and a user/ folder for overriding front-end files and server settings.
use_cases: host a shared movie or video night
share local video files with a small group
run a self-hosted CyTube-style watch party
how_to_run: Open the 'Local' link for yourself and send the 'Global' link to friends
Alternatively: docker build -t synctube . && docker run --rm -it -p 4200:4200 -v ${PWD}/user:/app/user synctube
Optional cache feature: npm i, plus ffmpeg/ffprobe installed on the server
notable: Leader button system for global playback control, with optional requestLeaderOnPause and unpauseWithoutLeader settings
Time-rewind chat commands such as /30, /-21 and /ad to skip YouTube sponsor blocks
Start playing local files while they are still uploading
Links mask like foo.com/bar${1-4}.mp4 to add multiple items at once
Front-end files can be overridden through the user/res folder
caveats: Server-side caching requires installing ffmpeg/ffprobe and an extra npm step; the default cache size is 3.0 GiB
Docker setup hides real local and global IPs, so these must be checked manually
Platform-as-a-service hosts without permanent storage need extra configuration to avoid sleeping and to keep user config
